topic: The Congo River is the only major river to cross the Equator twice: the upper river (Lualaba) flows north across the Equator near Kisangani, the great bend carries it west, and it recrosses the Equator southbound near Mbandaka before reaching the Atlantic (Britannica; NASA Earth Observatory). Length about 4,700 km, second-largest discharge after the Amazon at about 41,000 m³/s (Britannica; USGS). It is the deepest river known: USGS measurements in the lower Congo in 2008 found depths exceeding 220 m (Oberg et al., USGS 2009; Britannica). The Amazon runs mostly a few degrees south of the Equator and the Nile begins near the Equator at Lake Victoria but flows north away from it. Kinshasa (DR Congo) and Brazzaville (Republic of the Congo) face each other across Pool Malebo, the closest pair of national capitals in the world (Britannica).
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.
